newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy rate cut legitimate with CPI fall - minister.
newsitem.headline: Italy rate cut legitimate with CPI fall - minister.

text.p: Italy could legitimately expect a rate cut if April inflation is in line with preliminary data, Industry Minister Pier Luigi Bersani said.
Preliminary data from six Italian cities published earlier on Monday pointed to inflation falling to 1.8 percent year-on-year in April from 2.2 percent in March.
"If confirmed, we could legitimately expect a further fall in interest rates, which production needs," Bersani said in a statement.
He said Manday's data encouraged the government to push ahead with plans to reorganise the petrol distribution market.
"By rationalising the network and stimulating competition we could consolidate the effect on prices we have already started to see from today's data," Bersani said.
State controlled energy group ENI cut pump prices at self-service stations at the end of last month in a move later followed by other distributors.
Five other cities are due to release preliminary inflation data on Tuesday. Final CPI data will be published on May 6.
The Bank of Italy, which is independent of government control, cut the discount rate to 6.75 percent in January.
Unions and business leaders on Monday joined calls for further monetary easing in the wake of the inflation data. -- Rome newsroom +396 678 2501
